verdicts.verdict: CARNELIAN is the most coherent room system. It wins 7 of 14 screens (graveyard, hedge, study, crypt, greenhouse, sleeping quarters, and the nursery and graveyard fights), and it is the only candidate that steadily puts drawn, shadowed objects on the middle and near floor while keeping the ceiling and walls in frame. Its one serious defect is in fight-party at 1600, where Bones stands on a green chair back at near-left. That must be fixed before it ships. OBSIDIAN wins the foyer room, the foyer fight and the party fight with better floor lighting and clear fighter footing, but a Celtic cross sits on a Courage bar in fight-graveyard and its crypt, study and hedge are back-row rooms. AGATE wins nursery, pumpkin and passages by spreading objects across the floor, but it crops its big pieces at the frame edges and leaves wide bare stretches elsewhere. BASALT is the bare baseline: back-row dressing, cameras tilted down so ceilings are lost, and an unnamed translucent smear in the graveyard. None of the four is close to the painted hand of the references. Rooms sit at 4-6.5 and fights at 5.6-6.8.

verdicts.verdict: CARNELIAN is the most coherent room system. Across both tracks it most often puts drawn objects with shadows on the middle and near floor, and it keeps ceilings and side walls in frame (graveyard, greenhouse, crypt, study, sleeping, hedge). It wins 12 of 14 screens; AGATE takes nursery and pumpkin narrowly. In the fights, CARNELIAN's rooms stay furnished around and behind the fighters, and nothing a fighter stands on or through is worse than a lamp behind the Coatrack Crawler's legs at 1280. AGATE has a real collision: a Celtic cross rises out of the Coatrack Crawler's head under its DEBUFF sign. OBSIDIAN's headstones crowd the graveyard Courage bars. BASALT is consistently the barest: everything sits on the back wall, ceilings are cropped, and the graveyard has a nameless translucent smear. None reaches the reference paintings' hand. Bare near-floor strips remain in pumpkin, passages and foyer, and the foyer and greenhouse floors fall to black at the back. No screen meets coherence 9.

builds.notes_for_merger:
What changed (3 commits on ui/r59-rooms-a, base 5e4e3886, only fx/backdrop.js, fx/atmosphere.js and tests/grounding/):
1. CLEARANCE RULE (backdrop.js). I measured the sole line from CombatScene._stageFl across 10 window sizes and 6 encounter shapes. Script is tests/grounding/soles.py. Only window HEIGHT moves it, because the hand is a fixed pixel size: boss .457-.683, everyone else .514-.715. That gives SOLE_LINES, plus soleBand(innerHeight) at build time. A piece is in the way only when its foot sits below the band's top line, its head sits above the band's bottom line, and its end lies inside the fighters' reach. Reach is measured too: right REACH_RIGHT 1.22 half-heights; left 0.92 x aspect, with aspect held at 16:9 or wider. A piece that is in the way goes to whichever is the shortest move: forward of everyone's feet (low pieces only, kept on their line from the lens), out to the right edge (toTheEdge), or back behind the fight with a seeded spread so pieces do not form a rank.
   - Grave headstones and lamp standards now go through the same rule. A lamp moves its pal.lights entry and any nearFloor pool within 3 m with it.
   - Resize: a room is placed for the window it was built in. Backdrop._standAside(sole, aspect) reads the live sole line from Atmosphere._syncActors each tick. It collapses any piece the new line now stands in (instance scale 0, shadows included) and restores it when the window comes back.
2. CAMERA (stageRig). Square rigs now cast the measured stance (STANCE) at the real aspect, held to at least 16:9, and allow the floor to run R.w/2 + floorOver - 0.05. When the floor test fails, the eye comes down in 5 cm steps (floor STAGE_EYE_MIN 0.95) with the wall foot held on STAGE_BASE. It only pitches after that. Pools and non-square vantages keep the old 0.96-at-aspect-2 stance, so the Greenhouse gallery frames as before.
   - Wall foot is back at .39 in Sleeping and Attic, .38 in Crypt, .35 in Hedge, .335 in Passages (all were .16-.28). Crypt and Passages eyes are now 0.97 m.
3. LIGHT: a pool2 on the middle floor for the parlour kind (ahead 16.5), study (10.6) and nursery (pool widened to 6.2).
4. GRAVEYARD: the translucent arch in BASALT was a stone's ghost. It is gone, and two solid near stones (hand-flagged) now stand on the remaining moonlit patch.
5. NEW NEAR PIECES, all drawn from shapes already in each wing's PROP_SHAPES, so no new programs: pumpkins and a straw bale across the court's near flags, book piles in the study, low charnel mounds in the crypt, a toy box in the dormitory.
6. TEST (tests/grounding/run.py). It no longer skips graves, slabs or standing fixtures. It tests each actor across 0.8 of its shadow radius. Any stood-down piece must have scale exactly 0. Six rooms were added: parlor boss, nursery x4, yard x3, catacomb x4, dormitory x3, courtyard x4. PASS on all of them. `--original` runs only the old four.

Not done:
- Item 5 (hedge cells and flagstone softness) is shader work and was not attempted. The hedge only got its camera back.
- No shader files were edited and no prop program changed, so there was no getProgramInfoLog to read.

Verified:
- grounding PASS (checks.json committed; the regenerated checked-*.png were restored so ~32 MB of churn is not committed).
- tests/chrome 27/0 errors, steam-deck 6 passed, combat-scene seam 22 passed.
- gpuprof graveyard fight at 1600x900: T_full 13.3 ms. This is one reading, under the 15.5 ms budget.

Capture caveat:
- capture.py's 900 s subprocess timeout expired twice while waiting in the GPU queue behind other builders.
- The canonical PNGs were therefore made with capture.py's exact commands, run without the timeout: the same room_batch line (`--tier medium --w 1280 --h 800 --prefix OBSIDIAN-room-`), and the same shot.py arguments as its FIGHTS table. The runner is a copy of that table without the timeout.
- All 18 PNGs were looked at. None are void, and there are no console.txt files.

Known risk:
- At 1920x1080 a room built for 1024x768 stands aside many near pieces (the test counted 18 in the yard). A room entered at 1080p is placed for 1080p, so a player only sees this after resizing mid-fight.
- At 1080p and above the near floor is legitimately emptier, because the sole line sits lower.

builds.notes_for_merger:
WHAT CHANGED
1. The clearance rule (backdrop.js). The static pass that walked every floor piece back until its foot was above 42.5% of the screen is gone, along with the now-unused onStage, stageLens and stageShift. In its place Backdrop#stageAside(boxes, camera) is called from the new Atmosphere#_stageAside, which hangs off _syncActors. It "strikes" a floor piece (scale set to 0 on the piece, its contact shadow and its SHADOW_EXTRA pools, the same mechanism as _handCull) only while two things are both true: the piece's projected quad (10% inset) crosses a fighter's box (.cb-hero rect down to its shadow, each living .cb-enemy rect including its plate, and .cb-incoming), and the piece's foot is not at least 0.012 of the frame behind that fighter's sole line. Pieces it never touches: hang, arch, fixture, hand, and anything with y > 1. The boxes are re-read when a signature changes (canvas size, enemy count, hero count, placed count, room seed) and otherwise every 1.5 s. So resizing, summons and deaths re-place within one sync, and lunges never cause flicker. Pieces put themselves back when the fighter leaves. Empty rooms strike nothing, which is why they look like survey 10's again.
2. The camera (stageRig). The pitch loop now casts measured standing positions, STANDS = [[sole, aspect*|nx|]] = [.47,1.0] [.513,1.25] [.53,1.5] [.556,1.62] [.62,2.05]. These were measured with a geometry probe over every board shape (1 to 5 enemies, elite, boss, party) at 1280x800, 1600x900, 1920x1080, 1024x768 and 2560x1080. It replaces nx 0.96 at aspect 2 on a 44vh line. Crypt, Passages, Sleeping, Attic and Hedge get their vaults, end walls and skies back, and the 4-enemy corridor still passes.
3. The graveyard shader (fx/shaders/backdrop.js, MM_R25W 4). The translucent grey shape was the near end of SPHENE's trodden path p1, which started 4.5 m from the eye. It now starts at 12 m. The crisp rank-grass patch, a black shape on the open near lawn, is limited to the lawn's sides (|across| > 4 to 6.5 m) as its comment intended.
4. Rooms dressed by hand:
- Nursery: the toy chest moved upstage of every sole line, so it stays at the Kid's back in fights. The fire's glow (pool2) is laid on the middle boards.
- Parlour: lamps i:2 moved to x 6.4 / z 0.30, taking the lantern standard off the Kid's shoulder to the fight's right wing.
- Churchyard: footlights, a kerbed grave and a low stone, both marked still and hand, so the yews and moon do not move.
- Study: the middle floor pool widened, and a book pile added on the middle floor.
- Passages: two crate stacks on the near boards.
- Hedge: the near urn moved to the bare right-hand verge. It is no longer hand-culled.
- Every addition is marked still, so no deal stream moved. One exception: an early graveyard addition without still moved the yews over the moon; it was caught and fixed.

PROOF
- tests/grounding/run.py (on_port 9592) passes. It covers 8 rooms x 3 sizes (added nursery, graveyard 4-enemy, foyer boss parlour, crypt 4-enemy). It now checks every drawn (unstruck) floor piece against each fighter's body box as well as the soles, and checks standing lamps against the soles.
- tests/combat-scene/seam.py: 22/0.
- tests/chrome: 26/27. The only failure is the harness's 60fps check (median 55) on a GPU three builders are sharing.
- tests/steam-deck: fails with screens timing out (lobby, map, combat, reward on my build; select first time). I started BASE 5e4e3886 on :9599 and ran the same test there: it fails worse (2 of 11 screens reached). This is machine load and D3D state, not this branch; :9599 was stopped afterwards.
- gpuprof --settle 14, fight-graveyard (the most props) at 1600x900: T_full 10.1 and 9.3 ms, under the 15.5 budget. The BASE server on :9590 was down, so there is no A/B.
- No console errors in any capture state.json.
- The floor program draws: the lawn's leaves, roots and turf render in every graveyard capture, and the only compile log is the usual X4000 warning.

CAVEATS
- capture.py's 600 s shot timeout includes time spent waiting for the GPU slot. Under three builders several shots returned 124, and capture.py then copies any stale shots/CODE-*.png it finds. I deleted the stale ones and re-ran only the failed screens with capture.py ONLY. All 18 PNGs in CARNELIAN/ are from this build (14:58 to 16:52) and I looked at every one.
- Rooms outside the track were checked visually in a room_batch: kitchens, attic, lampworks, ballroom, bathhouse, kennels, heart. Title and map were photographed on :9592 and looked at.
- The crypt's floor-painted open graves still lie under the corridor fight's creatures, as on BASE. They are not props, so stageAside cannot strike them.

builds.notes_for_merger:
THE ANGLE IS CAMERA FIRST. Measured before changing anything (scratchpad soles.py: 6 window shapes, normal/elite/boss, 0-6 creatures). The highest sole is 0.457 of the screen height. Measured in half-heights from the middle, the furthest anyone stands is the Companion at -0.86 x aspect (left) and a creature at +1.05 (right, the same at every width). The last plate reaches 1.22.

1) stageRig (atmosphere.js) now asks the frame for floor at exactly those two points, at a 0.45 sole line, instead of nx +-0.96 at aspect>=2. It holds a margin up to 1.85:1. Atmosphere#_reRig rebuilds the room once if a window is dragged wider than that. STAGE_BASE goes from 0.39 to 0.41, and a vantage may set its own (kind.stageBase; the yard uses 0.35). Shells were reshaped for their ceilings: nursery h 4.0; sleeping 11x3.9 with the eye back; study eye +4 m, h 5.8, key and fill moved back with it, and a new pal.frameDz so its near frame stays behind the eye; crypt w13; passages w8.8; hedge w13 with a lower eye; parlour h x0.82 and lens 0.96.

2) The clearance rule (Backdrop onStage) keeps a piece only if it is BEHIND (foot <= 0.445), LOW (its whole height >= 0.635, under the lowest sole at 1920x1080), or OUT RIGHT (left edge >= 1.25 half-heights). Everything else walks back as before. A walked piece then goes on back by a hashed share of the floor left behind it, so pieces no longer stand in one rank. Its tone is lifted to >=0.8, because a layout's darkened front rank was turning into black cut-outs. Graves now walk too: a Kid was standing through a Crypt headstone. Standing lamp fittings walk back together with their light.

3) nearFloor.mid is a pool measured from the rig, from the far wall's foot to the soles. It is set in 9 of the 10 rooms (greenhouse unchanged).

4) Graveyard: the translucent grey shape is the empty room's NEAR FRAME clutter band. It stayed in the same screen place under every camera, and props=0 did not remove it. The yard's vantage now has frame:'none' (fights already ran fightFrame:false). The yard looks further down, a lantern now stands among the rows, and the near stones are hand-placed. The black dithered jags left of the walk are still there and I could not name their source.

5) Near-floor dressing uses the round-39 `hand` flag (culled while a fight stands) for tall pieces under the cards. Survey 10's pumpkins come forward across the flags this way. Low pieces and right-zone pieces stay in fights.

TESTS (all run through on_port 9593): tests/grounding PASS on 15 cases x 3 sizes. I added nursery, yard, parlour boss, parlour with 4 creatures, dormitory with 4, catacomb, hedge, courtyard, conservatory and library. The test is STRONGER, not weaker: it now checks both ends of each footprint, and it no longer exempts graves, slabs or fittings. That surfaced a real pre-existing collision, the Conservatory's fountain lamp, which is fixed. I raised the cold-room timeout from 90 to 300 s and the post-resize wait from 1.3 to 2.6 s: the plates refit at 2.2 s, and under three builders the 1024 case read mid-refit. combat-scene/seam 22/22. chrome 26/27: the one fail is 60fps (median 33) on a machine shared by three capturers, not code. steam-deck 5/7: lobby did not come up (TimeoutError), so 10 of 11 screens. Lobby is not mine and was not re-run. gpuprof --settle 14: fight-nursery T_full 14.38 ms, fight-graveyard 14.27 ms, one reading each under load. linkprof on the floor programs: 26 programs, worst 12.1 s, every link true; the proglog link status in gpuprof is also true.

Captures: capture.py's own 900 s timeout counts time spent queued for the GPU slot and killed my first run. I took the canonical set with an untimed copy (scratchpad capture_nt.py): same commands, same arguments, same output names. Off-track screens, photographed and looked at: title, shop, default combat (stair hall).
